Buffer ugen::absdif ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::absdif(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Definition at line 110 of file ugen_BinaryOpUGens.cpp.

Buffer ugen::absdif ( const float  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the rightOperand and have the same number of channels. The constant leftOperand will be applied to all channels and values using the absdif() function.

See also:
Buffer::absdif(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Buffer ugen::fold ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::fold(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Definition at line 96 of file ugen_BinaryOpUGens.cpp.

Buffer ugen::fold ( const float  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the rightOperand and have the same number of channels. The constant leftOperand will be applied to all channels and values using the fold() function.

See also:
Buffer::fold(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Buffer ugen::pow ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::pow(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Buffer ugen::sqrdif ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::sqrdif(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Definition at line 109 of file ugen_BinaryOpUGens.cpp.

Buffer ugen::sqrdif ( const float  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the rightOperand and have the same number of channels. The constant leftOperand will be applied to all channels and values using the sqrdif() function.

See also:
Buffer::sqrdif(Buffer const& rightOperand)
